assumptions: source assumption: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium conditions stated on the page: an infinitely large population with no mutations, migration, emigration, or selective pressure for or against genotype.

source assumption: exactly two alleles at one diploid locus with p + q = 1, random mating, and offspring genotypes formed by the random union of two gene-pool alleles (random mating explicit in the AP edition condition list: 'no mutations, no gene flow, random mating, no genetic drift, and no selection'; implicit in Biology 2e via 'if we draw two alleles at random from the gene pool').

models.inverse_notes: Allele frequency is recoverable as the nonnegative root of fAA (p = +sqrt(fAA)); the negative root is rejected by the p >= 0 guard. Substitution check: fAA = 0.64 gives p = 0.8, consistent with the violet-flower reference. Boundary p = 0 gives fAA = 0 (allele absent from the gene pool) and is admissible, not a violation. Joint inversion of (p, q) from fAA alone is underdetermined and not attempted.
limitations: Predicts the expected genotype frequency under equilibrium; a real population whose measured frequency deviates is evolving (drift, mutation, migration, selection).
Excludes loci with more than two alleles, sex linkage, polyploidy and nonrandom mating; the source notes no natural population fully satisfies the equilibrium conditions.

models.inverse_notes: Given fAa and nonzero p, q = fAa / (2p), symmetric in p and q. Substitution check: fAa = 0.32 with p = 0.8 gives q = 0.2, consistent with the violet-flower reference. Zero-factor boundary: p = 0 or q = 0 gives fAa = 0 (one allele fixed); admissible, not a violation. Recovering a unique (p, q) pair from fAa alone is underdetermined and not attempted. The sum-to-one condition p + q = 1 is kept as an assumption, not an executable guard, to avoid floating-point equality on rounded published inputs.
limitations: Predicts the expected genotype frequency under equilibrium; a measured deviation means the population is evolving.
Excludes loci with more than two alleles, sex linkage, polyploidy and nonrandom mating.

models.inverse_notes: Any one allele frequency is recoverable given all others (e.g. f1 = 1 - f2 - f3); the record fixes f3 as output only as the serialization choice. Substitution check: 1 - 0.261 - 0.134 = 0.605, consistent with the ABO reference. Fixation of one allele (the rest zero) gives 1 and is admissible.
limitations: Multi-allele loci only in the three-allele serialization; loci with more alleles need the fuller summation, not recorded here.
A bookkeeping complement, not an equilibrium prediction; it holds regardless of evolutionary forces.
Published percentage triples may not sum to exactly 100.0 (the mosquito pre-treatment triple sums to 99.9); affected references carry the rounding in their tolerances.

references.method: Published Jordanian ABO study figures quoted on the page: IA 26.1 percent and IB 13.4 percent leave 1 - 0.261 - 0.134 = 0.605 for I0, matching the quoted 60.5 percent.
